fixes.explanation: You got it, baker. "And sitting down, He taught the people from the boat." (Luke 5:3). Luke 5:2 says the fishermen were washing their nets. Now Simon's boat is where the teaching happens.

Nope, friend, not yet anyway. Simon says they "…worked hard all night without catching anything." (Luke 5:5). That night gave them nothing to sell. A big catch does come later in the passage (Luke 5:6), but only after Jesus speaks.
Not quite, baker. Simon doesn't mention any storm. He says they "…worked hard all night without catching anything." (Luke 5:5). What he tells Jesus about is hard work and no fish.

That's it, baker. Simon says, "But because You say so, I will let down the nets." (Luke 5:5). After a night like that, I'd have OPINIONS about letting those nets down again. Simon gives one reason, and it's what Jesus said.

Good guess, baker, but Simon doesn't give that reason. He says, "But because You say so, I will let down the nets." (Luke 5:5). I'd love a fish forecast too, but Simon doesn't hand one out. He points to what Jesus said.

Not quite, friend. Jesus is the one who tells Simon, "Put out into deep water and let down your nets for a catch." (Luke 5:4). Simon answers, "But because You say so, I will let down the nets." (Luke 5:5). His reason is what Jesus said, not a request from his partners.
YES, baker! After a whole night of nothing, "…they caught such a large number of fish that their nets began to tear." (Luke 5:6). Nothing all night, and then nets ripping. Talk about a turnaround!

You got it, baker. "…they signaled to their partners in the other boat to come and help them…" (Luke 5:7). The nets are tearing, so they wave over the other boat. Then both boats get filled so full that they begin to sink.
That's right, baker. "When Simon Peter saw this, he fell at Jesus’ knees." (Luke 5:8). The boats are full and sinking, and what Simon Peter does is drop down in front of Jesus.

That's right, baker. Simon Peter says, "Go away from me, Lord, for I am a sinful man" (Luke 5:8). Luke 5:9 says he and his companions were astonished at the catch of fish. I think this is a heavy moment for him, and I'd just let his words stand.

Yes, baker. Simon, his companions and his partners James and John are astonished at the catch, and Jesus says to Simon, "Do not be afraid…" (Luke 5:9-10). Simon had just fallen at His knees, so those words land right where he is. Short, plain and kind.

Not quite, baker. Simon, his companions and his partners James and John are astonished at the catch (Luke 5:9-10). Jesus does speak to Simon, and He says, "Do not be afraid…" (Luke 5:10). He says it plainly to Simon.
That's right, baker. Jesus says, "From now on you will catch men." (Luke 5:10). Simon is out fishing, and Jesus tells him what's ahead. The words "From now on…" tell us it's a new start.
